description: Bulldogs Beyond Earth is a team of PhD students from the University of Georgia, united by a passion for space exploration, innovation, and discovery. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to transform creative ideas into meaningful solutions for real challenges in lunar exploration. Driven by curiosity, collaboration, and a shared ambition to explore new frontiers, we welcome enthusiastic individuals who believe that the next great discovery begins with bold ideas and teamwork.

details:
WHAT IT DOES

Lunar Landing Site Navigator turns NASA terrain and ephemeris data into a quick mission decision for the lunar south pole. A user picks Artemis III candidate regions, a landing date and a stay length. Every 10 minutes the app works out whether the Sun and Earth are above the real LOLA terrain horizon at each site. It reports sunlight %, direct-to-Earth contact % (gated by Deep Space Network station visibility), the longest dark period and Earth gap, an illustrative battery size, and how each result changes if the landing slips 24 or 48 hours. Sites are ranked by their worst-case score, and ties are shown as ties. A Best Date Finder ranks the best landing dates from 2026 to 2031. A 3D observer view shows the Sun and Earth over real terrain from any site.

HOW IT WORKS

Sun and Earth positions come from NASA/JPL NAIF SPICE kernels (DE421, lunar frame) via Skyfield, in the same frame as the LOLA DEMs. Terrain horizons are ray-cast to 150 km over the LOLA 80 m and 240 m south-pole DEMs, including lunar curvature. The finite Sun and Earth discs and lunar eclipses are modeled. Results that missing terrain could change are flagged and not recommended.

VALIDATION

Sun and Earth positions match JPL Horizons to 0.00001° at all 8 sites. Physics checks pass, including known eclipse dates, and 34 automated tests pass.

EXAMPLE

For a landing on Aug 16, 2027, Malapert Massif, de Gerlache Rim 2 and Mons Mouton all score 100 on time. A 48-hour slip drops Malapert to 86, while the other two stay at 100.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Planners get a defensible answer in seconds instead of combining Horizons, SPICE and terrain tools by hand. Students and the public can see why the low south-polar Sun and the wobbling Earth make site and date choices hard.

TOOLS

Python, Skyfield, NumPy, pandas, rasterio, pyproj, GeoPandas, Streamlit, Plotly, pytest, GitHub, Streamlit Community Cloud.

LIMITATIONS

The model is line of sight only. It has no hazard or slope map, no thermal model and no radio link budget, and the power values are illustrative.
